answers-lazy.comment: PINNED 2026-08-28. Twenty of two thousand rows, abandoned, fifty times over. The inference pin is ZERO and that zero is the case: bridge.pl's metta_node_guarded/2 reports what a job spent as that job's LAST event, reached only once the command has no more answers, so an abandoned job contributes nothing. A lazy path that began draining would report query-rows' 282622 and fail this row by four orders of magnitude, and the workload's own crossing bound fails first at 1600. Instructions carry the SIZE, since a counter fixed at zero cannot say whether twenty rows cost twenty rows' work or two thousand; most of what they price is the teardown, because leaving the loop early closes the cursor and destroys the engine behind it. Fifty abandonments rather than one because a two millisecond window spread 0.2763 percent across nine samples against a one percent band. Inferences identical in all 9 samples of 3 consecutive runs; instructions spread 0.0399 percent over 9 samples of 3 consecutive runs [measured 2026-08-28: minimum of [815818054, 815831092, 815774521]; command=CHECK_PY=<an interpreter with janus_swi> sh extensions/node/bench.sh --update; fixture=swipl-wasm 8.0.6 on node 22.22.1 (V8 12.4.254.21-node.35), the compiled TypeScript build, box under loadavg 9 with another gate running; commit=0f6803e2377036ae526474434851b7a592f04703] RE-PINNED 2026-08-28 for a HARNESS fix, not a code change: every instruction row moved at once and every inference row stayed identical, which is the signature of the measurement rather than the work. benchmarks/sampler.ts now collects the heap to a fixed point at the end of setup, outside the window, under a fourth V8 flag `--expose-gc`. The three flags already there make a run reproducible against ITSELF; this makes it reproducible against a CHANGED PROGRAM. `--predictable-gc-schedule` is deterministic given the same allocation sequence and the startup heap is part of that sequence, so growing any module the benchmark loads shifted where a collection landed inside the window. Measured rather than argued, by a probe that cannot possibly do work: four kilobytes of INERT COMMENTS added to src/theory.ts moved host-op from 900018262 to 933434511, a 3.7 percent phantom regression from text nothing executes, and the same probe against the settled heap moves the whole suite at most 0.18 percent (atom-intern), with host-op at 0.016 percent. The rows that went UP now carry the collections their own allocation causes instead of inheriting an accidental share of the startup heap's, which is why answers-lazy and query-rows rose while host-op and atom-intern fell. This is the layout-bias class Mytkowicz et al. name, and a settled starting heap is the cheap half of Stabilizer's answer to it [source: Mytkowicz, Diwan, Hauswirth and Sweeney, "Producing Wrong Data Without Doing Anything Obviously Wrong!", ASPLOS 2009; Curtsinger and Berger, "Stabilizer", ASPLOS 2013]. This row moved 814157514 to 1015712124 in that one step [measured 2026-08-28; command=sh extensions/node/bench.sh --update; fixture=swipl-wasm 8.0.6 on node 22.22.1 (V8 12.4.254.21-node.35), the compiled TypeScript build; commit=57f21ba9edf94bcf28cde11f938bce2c241a3709]. The inference pin remains zero, proving all fifty asks are still abandoned; retired instructions moved 1015712124 to 938757435, down 76954689, with update samples [939015332, 938757435, 939084889]. answers-lazy.not_reproducible_here_2026_09_20_comment: NOT REPRODUCIBLE ON THIS BOX, 2026-09-20, and the pin STANDS. This row reads a different number here than the one committed, deterministically, in every tree provenance tried: a battery (rsync copy), the long-lived checkout, a `git worktree` at the submodule mount's parent, and a FRESH CLONE at b88bfb4ce with its submodules populated from the component remotes and its own `npm run build`. define-call reads 86785 against its 86353 in all three samples of all four; host-op 81452 against 81467 and query-rows 238907 against 238969, both improvements; answers-lazy, host-op and query-rows instruction minima all below their pins. Eliminated by controlled reversal, each arm re-provisioned and measured: the engine alone at the pin's gitlink, engine with lib, the benchmark harness alone, and engine with lib with harness with the Python seat together; the node seat's own three commits in the range touch only llms.txt, a .gitignore and the runner scripts. Both MORK objects and engine/reader.so were placed in every arm, and the configuration stamp matches on all five fields, swipl-wasm 8.0.6 and node v22.22.1 among them. The lib-alone arm refusing to boot is what says the arms reach the code they name. The 2026-09-06 release re-pin met the same shape and ruled the same way: the number is the measurement environment rather than the engine, the pin stands, and the note beside it says which trees read what. Re-pinning was considered and refused, because no mechanism survived measurement and a pin moved without one is the fabrication this repository's benchmark protocol exists to prevent. What remains unaccounted for is the box, not the tree.

define-call.comment: PINNED 2026-08-28. Five hundred host calls of a lowered `define`d body, 477.01 inferences a call. The body is lowered, so the whole of it lives in the engine and a call costs no host crossing per step; what this prices is the per-call path, the ask out and the one answer back. Inferences alone decide, because the host's share is one ask per call and is already the smallest this door can be. The countdown body is comparison-led recursion: `==` is now total term equality, the translator gives total booleans the final-result shape, and an engine with no configured max-stack-depth emits no default fuel charge. patched_wasm_host_restamp_comment: RE-STAMPED 2026-09-23 for the host, and no pin moved. The seat now boots the patched WebAssembly SWI-Prolog it carries in _host/ instead of npm's swipl-wasm 8.0.6, so swipl_wasm names that host's bytes, a sha256 over swipl-web.cjs, swipl-web.wasm and swipl-web.data, and every pin had to be checked against the new configuration. Measured on one box in one battery, whole suite, three samples a row, as four arms differing in one thing each: A, this seat before the change on npm's host; B, the same seat on the patched host; D, this change; E, this change without its boot check. Inferences: A reads answers-lazy 0, define-call 87285, host-op 81453 and query-rows 238908; B reads the same four, so no defect fix and nothing else in the host moves an inference row; D reads the same except query-rows 238907, and E reads 238908, so that one inference is the boot check's: its partition/4 over a module-qualified closure pays at boot one of the 165 inferences the workload's first run otherwise pays, and three runs on one engine read 238908, 238743, 238743 without the check and 238907, 238743, 238743 with it, so the steady state is unchanged. Instructions, D against A: answers-lazy -0.69 percent, atom-intern -0.94, host-op -0.68, query-rows -0.80, wire-roundtrip -0.08. The host-side rows move with the seat's module layout, since B equals A on them, and the engine-side rows with the host binary, B against A reading -0.87, -0.70 and -1.04. Every move is inside its row's declared band, 4 inferences or 1 percent of instructions, so every pin stands by this file's rule that a pin whose row stayed inside its band is not replaced. This box reads define-call, host-op and query-rows away from their pins under A as well (87285, 81453 and 238908 against 86353, 81467 and 238969), which is the discrepancy the 2026-09-20 note on define-call records; it is the same in every arm and is left as that note leaves it. That the deltas measured here hold where the pins were taken is assumed, not measured [measured 2026-09-23: BATTERY_SOURCE=<arm> sh tools/battery.sh run 4 -- sh -c 'cd extensions/node && npm run build && cd ../.. && sh extensions/node/bench.sh --update' per arm; fixture=node 22.22.1 (V8 12.4.254.21-node.35) under loadavg 18 to 27; commit=b18f7d31d58691f97112d0de67b0136bfd8a3291].

release_0_7_0_layout_repin_comment: RE-PINNED 2026-09-04 for the 0.7.0 release work. Instruction-only, and the evidence that it is LAYOUT rather than work is that the inference counts are byte-identical across three samples on every row that pins one: query-rows 238914, define-call 85386, host-op 79387. answers-lazy pins ZERO inferences by design -- an abandoned job reports nothing -- so it cannot carry that evidence itself, and it moved by the same proportion in the same process as query-rows, which can. The engine image grew this session -- a seam declaration, the tracer's truncation flag and cell budget, the fast-cache scan's clauses -- and qlf_boot.pl regenerates the umbrella QLF files, so the same logical work is reached through differently placed code. That is the same mechanism this file already records for the provenance-only WORKTREE replacement that moved the MORK control-window floor 28313 to 28808. No row's inference count moved [measured 2026-09-04; command=sh extensions/node/bench.sh --update; fixture=warm main-checkout engine artifacts; commit=2716538842ed9cdf0b85bcf0e3acec32b092c3ee]
release_0_8_0_repin_comment:
RE-PINNED 2026-09-06 for the 0.8.0 release. Five numbers across four rows.

The three instruction rows are one commit. 82c1ab65, the typing-rule scope fix, moves host-op 915,889,424 to 1,001,080,939 (+9.3%), answers-lazy +2.0% and query-rows +1.3%; two independent ladder runs agree on that step, and the second is what settles it, because the first run's reading at the tip fell back by the same amount and did not reproduce. 26f479ba's query planning gives answers-lazy -0.4%. The two rows that decide on instructions alone, atom-intern and wire-roundtrip, moved -0.309% and +0.002% inside their 1% bands and keep their pins.

The two inference rows are NOT attributed, and the reason is stated rather than guessed. define-call 85262 to 86265 (+1003, two per call over 500 calls) and host-op 79387 to 81396 (+2009, one per yield over 2,000 yields) already read those values at a94f804c, so both moved before this pass's sweep base; the 2026-09-05 sweep records define-call moving twice in that earlier window, at b1eed73d and at 8bd37f30's fixed-width catalog selection, and this pass could not extend the bisect to them because `npm run build` exits 2 at every commit in that range against the node_modules this seat has now. So: moved between dd158bf5 and a94f804c, not attributed.

wall_seconds_per_operation is restored to its committed value for every row: wall advises in this file's own counter policy, and the box carried loadavg 12 to 19 through the pass.

v8_flag_note: Every instructions row is measured under the v8_flags in the stamp. A Node process is not deterministic enough to gate on retired instructions without them: bare, one engine workload spread 29.48 percent over four rounds, --liftoff-only alone took it to 2.55 percent and named the mechanism as TurboFan tiering swipl-wasm up on background threads inside the window, and the full set reaches 0.027 percent. These rows therefore measure Liftoff-compiled WebAssembly and single-threaded V8 rather than the tier a long-lived process settles into, which is the right trade for a gate that reads the change [measured 2026-08-28].
